assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, the proglucagon-derived peptide's insulinotropic and satiety actions) led to receptor agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional; the story runs from basic peptide physiology to a major medicine.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiological characterisation of GLP-1 secretion and action) and Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor pharmacology, translation) are the clearest scientific anchors. Knudsen is the leading credited figure for developing long-acting, clinically usable analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide is a contested credit question; I rely on the supplied credit rather than having verified the priority dispute.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of replication, large randomised outcome trials and widespread clinical use make recognition timely, arguably overdue as a transformative therapy.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Drucker, Holst, Knudsen, Mojsov (and others outside the list) is unresolved and a three-person limit forces a choice.
Whether the committee prefers to honour physiology or the drug development is uncertain; I have not independently verified priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Clarity and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (medicinal chemistry and kinase inhibitor programme), Druker (preclinical demonstration and clinical trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a coherent, widely recognised trio. Fusion-protein and Philadelphia chromosome discovery by others is already part of earlier recognition; I am not fully certain of the prizes' prior coverage.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: two decades of survival data, independent confirmation and class generalisation to other kinases.
uncertainties: Whether Sawyers' resistance work or other chemists at the originating company deserve inclusion over a listed name is uncertain.
Prior prizes (for oncogenes and chromosome translocation) may weigh on how the committee frames this.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, a rare case of cancer prevention by vaccination with population-level effect now documented in vaccinated cohorts. It builds on, and complements, the earlier recognition of HPV as a cause of cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 virus-like particles at the NCI; Frazer (with colleagues including the late Jian Zhou) developed the VLP expression and the Gardasil-related technology. Credit among these three is reasonably clear, though others contributed and the commercial vaccine development involved additional groups.
assessment.maturity: Mature: over 15 years of real-world data show strong reductions in infection, precancer and now invasive cancer in vaccinated populations; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Role of Jian Zhou (deceased) and other groups in the original VLP work could complicate the configuration.
Interaction with the prior zur Hausen prize and the 2023 vaccine prize may affect committee appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provides cell-type-specific, millisecond control of neural activity and has become a standard tool across neuroscience, enabling causal circuit dissection and early therapeutic applications such as vision restoration. Originality and methodological impact are very large.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment as a neuronal tool (Boyden, Deisseroth, with Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted light activation) are all decisive. Six credited names cannot fit within three; any selection omits important contributors, and I choose the discoverers of the channel plus the principal user-developer.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly confirmed across thousands of studies; clinical translation is still early, but the tool value alone is established.
uncertainties: Credit distribution among six names is the main barrier; Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck are strong alternatives.
The relative weight of channel discovery versus neuronal application is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defines how the endoplasmic reticulum signals stress to the nucleus, a fundamental principle of proteostasis with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory disease. It is conceptually clean and original.
assessment.attribution: Mori (yeast Ire1/Hac1 pathway and HAC1 mRNA processing) and Walter (Ire1 as the sensor, unconventional splicing, later ISRIB work) are the central figures; Peter Walter and Mori share a well-known pairing. Other contributors (e.g. Ron, Mori's collaborators) exist but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation across species; clinical translation is emerging rather than complete, which does not diminish the basic discovery.
uncertainties: Whether Ron's PERK/ATF4 branch work should be recognised is unresolved and not offered in the supplied list.
Disease-relevance claims for the UPR are partly still in development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, with striking clinical benefit in infants and proof that splice-switching oligonucleotides can treat genetic disease. From a neurological standpoint this is a compelling bench-to-bedside story.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a natural two-person allocation; contributions by Adrian Krainer's collaborators and by SMN gene discoverers (Melki, Lefebvre) are not part of the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: eight years of clinical use and long-term follow-up; the platform has been broadly confirmed but the field's full impact is still unfolding.
uncertainties: The role of SMN1 gene identification versus therapy development may need separate recognition.
Long-term durability data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have established a new class of living drugs, now extending to autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical development of CD19 CAR-T), Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and TIL concepts) are plausible principal contributors; early CAR concept originators (Eshhar, Gross) are outside the supplied credit, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature for hematologic cancers with confirmation across products, though toxicity, solid-tumour limits and relapse remain; timing is plausible but not obviously final.
uncertainties: Credit for early chimeric receptor work is outside the supplied names.
Durability and safety, and extension beyond B-cell cancers, are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signalling is the central regulator linking nutrients and growth factors to cell growth and metabolism, with implications for cancer, ageing, immunosuppression and diabetes. Concept and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR as the target of rapamycin in yeast and established its function; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and its complexes. Schreiber's contribution (FKBP12-rapamycin) is real but more chemical-biological and the supplied three-name list would dilute the core discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic biology and confirmed widely; clinical applications (rapalogs) are real but narrower than the biology, and Sabatini-related controversy in 2021 may affect committee appetite.
uncertainties: Sabatini's professional circumstances may weigh on a committee decision; I do not assess this further.
Roles of Sabers, Sabatini, Schreiber and Brown/Sabatini-era mammalian discovery by others (Sabatini and Brown) are not fully disentangled.
